title: The Miraculousness And Testimony Of The Quran 17th Degree Turning To The Quran And Referring To The Risale I Nur

questions.question: What did the traveller believe was the main purpose of life in this world?
questions.answer: He believed the real purpose and core of life is faith.

questions.question: What book did the traveller decide to study?
questions.answer: He decided to study the Qur'an.

questions.question: How is that book described at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: It is described as extremely well-known, full of light and wisdom, and unlike any other book.

questions.question: What special challenge does the Qur'an give to people in every age?
questions.answer: It challenges those who reject it to answer its claim and match it.

questions.question: Before studying what the Qur'an says, what did the traveller think had to be proven first?
questions.answer: He thought it first had to be shown that the Qur'an comes from the Creator.

questions.question: Because he lived in the present age, what did he examine first?
questions.answer: He examined the Risale-i Nur first.

questions.question: How are the parts of the Risale-i Nur described?
questions.answer: They are described as many sections that present bright insights and solid explanations taken from the Qur'an.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Risale-i Nur in an age of stubborn disbelief?
questions.answer: It says it spreads Qur'anic truths bravely and cannot be overcome.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does the strength of the Risale-i Nur show about the Qur'an?
questions.answer: It shows that the Qur'an is its source, guide, and highest authority, and that it is heavenly speech, not human speech.

questions.question: Which two places in the Risale-i Nur are mentioned as giving a strong proof of the Qur'an’s miraculous nature?
questions.answer: The Twenty-Fifth Word and the ending of the Nineteenth Letter.

questions.question: What effect do those proofs have on someone who studies them?
questions.answer: They lead the person to admire the reasoning instead of criticizing it.

questions.question: After mentioning these proofs, what did the traveller choose to do next?
questions.answer: He left the full proof to the Risale-i Nur and only pointed briefly to a few signs of the Qur'an’s greatness.

questions.question: Who was the traveller speaking to at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: He was speaking to his own heart.

questions.question: Why did the traveller want to look into the Qur'an?
questions.answer: He wanted to examine the book said to be the speech of the One they were seeking.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the Qur'an’s place in the world among books?
questions.answer: It presents the Qur'an as the most outstanding and wise book in the world.

questions.question: What does the Qur'an do toward people who refuse to yield to it?
questions.answer: It openly challenges them.

questions.question: What careful step did the traveller want to take before examining the Qur'an’s message?
questions.answer: He wanted first to confirm that it truly came from Allah.

questions.question: Why did the traveller turn first to the Risale-i Nur rather than somewhere else?
questions.answer: He did so because he was living in the current age.

questions.question: What relationship does the passage give between the Risale-i Nur and the Qur'an?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur is presented as drawing its light, explanations, and authority from the Qur'an.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the statement that no one can defeat the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: It suggests that the truth it carries is powerful and that its source is divine, not man-made.

questions.question: How many aspects of the Qur'an’s miraculous nature are said to be shown in one proof mentioned here?
questions.answer: Forty aspects.

questions.question: What response do these arguments create in fair-minded readers?
questions.answer: They move readers toward appreciation and praise.

questions.question: Did the traveller try to give every proof himself in this passage? Explain.
questions.answer: No. He left the detailed proof to the Risale-i Nur and gave only a short mention of a few points.

questions.question: According to him, what gives life its true meaning?
questions.answer: Faith gives life its true meaning.

questions.question: What two things did he want to learn about the Qur'an?
questions.answer: He wanted to know what it says and whether it truly comes from the Creator.

questions.question: How does the passage present the Qur'an’s challenge across time?
questions.answer: It says the challenge continues in every age, not only in the past.

questions.question: What does the traveller’s first step tell us about his attitude toward belief?
questions.answer: It shows he values evidence and wants belief to rest on proof.

questions.question: In the present age, what source did he use to begin his investigation?
questions.answer: He began with the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Risale-i Nur contains?
questions.answer: It contains many sections made up of insights from the Qur'an and sound explanations of its meanings.

questions.question: What contrast is made between the age and the Risale-i Nur’s work?
questions.answer: The age is described as stubborn and atheistic, yet the Risale-i Nur still spreads Qur'anic truths strongly.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from the fact that the Risale-i Nur cannot be defeated?
questions.answer: The conclusion is that the Qur'an behind it is from heaven and not from human beings.

questions.question: What is special about the proof found in the two named sections of the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: It explains many sides of the Qur'an’s miraculous character in a powerful way.

questions.question: How are readers expected to react after seeing that proof?
questions.answer: They are expected to respect it and praise its reasoning rather than object to it.

questions.question: Why does the traveller mention only a few signs of greatness at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: Because he leaves the fuller, detailed demonstration to the Risale-i Nur itself.

questions.question: What did the traveller already understand about life before beginning this examination?
questions.answer: He already understood that life’s aim and deepest reality are tied to faith.

questions.question: What was the name used in the passage for the Qur'an?
questions.answer: It was called the Qur'an of Miraculous Exposition.

questions.question: Whose speech was the Qur'an said to be?
questions.answer: It was said to be the speech of the Being the traveller was seeking.

questions.question: What shows that the traveller did not want to study carelessly?
questions.answer: He insisted on proving first that the Qur'an came from the Creator.

questions.question: What did he do after making that decision?
questions.answer: He began searching for evidence.

questions.question: What work did he look at first because of the time in which he lived?
questions.answer: He looked first at the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the connection between the Risale-i Nur and the Qur'an’s meanings?
questions.answer: It says the Risale-i Nur reflects rays from the Qur'an and explains its contents on firm grounds.

questions.question: What fact about the Risale-i Nur is used as evidence in this passage?
questions.answer: The fact that no one can overcome it even while it spreads Qur'anic truths in a difficult age.

questions.question: What does that evidence point to about the Qur'an?
questions.answer: It points to the Qur'an being the true source and a revelation from above, not a human product.

questions.question: What do the named sections of the Risale-i Nur accomplish regarding the Qur'an?
questions.answer: They show many dimensions of its miraculous nature.

questions.question: What did the traveller decide about presenting all those proofs himself?
questions.answer: He decided not to present all of them there and instead to mention only a few signs of the Qur'an’s greatness.

questions.question: What belief about faith shaped the traveller’s search?
questions.answer: He believed faith is the goal of life and the heart of real living.

questions.question: Why did he choose to examine the Qur'an?
questions.answer: He chose it because it is said to be the speech of the One he was seeking.

questions.question: What claim is made about the Qur'an compared with other books?
questions.answer: It is presented as the most famous, radiant, and wise book.

questions.question: What ongoing feature of the Qur'an is highlighted in the passage?
questions.answer: Its challenge continues through every age.

questions.question: What had to be settled before looking into the Qur'an’s teachings, according to the traveller?
questions.answer: It had to be settled that the Qur'an truly came from the Creator.

questions.question: What did the traveller use first as help in this investigation?
questions.answer: He used the Risale-i Nur first.

questions.question: What does the passage say the many sections of the Risale-i Nur are based on?
questions.answer: They are based on lights and explanations taken from the Qur'an.

questions.question: Why is the Risale-i Nur’s inability to be defeated important in the passage?
questions.answer: It is important because it serves as a sign that the Qur'an behind it is from Allah, not from people.

questions.question: What is said about the proof found in the Twenty-Fifth Word and the end of the Nineteenth Letter?
questions.answer: It presents forty strong signs of the Qur'an’s miraculous quality.

questions.question: What change in attitude does that proof bring to the viewer?
questions.answer: It turns criticism into admiration.

questions.question: In the end, what approach did the traveller take in this passage?
questions.answer: He relied on the Risale-i Nur for the full case and gave only a short introduction to a few points about the Qur'an’s greatness.

questions.question: At the beginning of the passage, what does the traveller say about the purpose and essence of life?
questions.answer: He says both are found in faith.

questions.question: Which book did he want to examine as part of his search?
questions.answer: He wanted to examine the Qur'an.

questions.question: What makes the Qur'an stand out in the passage’s description?
questions.answer: It stands out as a book known everywhere for its brilliance and wisdom.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the Qur'an’s relationship with those who reject it?
questions.answer: It says the Qur'an confronts them with a challenge in every age.

questions.question: What was the traveller’s first goal before studying the Qur'an’s message?
questions.answer: His first goal was to establish that it is from the Creator.

questions.question: What did the traveller examine first because he belonged to the present age?
questions.answer: He examined the Risale-i Nur first.

questions.question: How are the writings of the Risale-i Nur portrayed in relation to the Qur'an?
questions.answer: They are portrayed as explanations and reflections that come from the Qur'an’s light.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Risale-i Nur’s struggle in the modern age?
questions.answer: It says it spreads the truths of the Qur'an courageously in a resistant, unbelieving age.

questions.question: What conclusion does the traveller draw from the fact that no one can defeat it?
questions.answer: He concludes that the Qur'an is its true source and that the Qur'an is divine speech.

questions.question: What two sections are named as especially powerful for proving the Qur'an’s extraordinary nature?
questions.answer: The Twenty-Fifth Word and the closing part of the Nineteenth Letter.

questions.question: According to the passage, how do these arguments affect someone who understands them?
questions.answer: They lead that person to respect and praise the arguments instead of finding faults.

questions.question: Why does the passage end by saying the traveller will mention only a few points?
questions.answer: Because he leaves the detailed proof of the Qur'an’s miraculous nature to the Risale-i Nur.
